key_idea: Use the spectrum's autocorrelation (diffraction) measure, a construction from mathematical diffraction theory, to turn spectrality into a weak tiling of the complement of Ω by translates of Ω, then use convex geometry to show that weak tiling forces a polytope that tiles face-to-face.
reason: The reduction from spectral to weak tiling through Hof-style autocorrelation measures is conceptual, surprising and reusable, and the polytope step (infinitely many normals give disjoint support sets, each carrying mass at least 1) is clean. However, the second half rests on a long chain of local lemmas about facets, subfacets, belts and o(δ) volume estimates, which adds a lot of geometric bookkeeping.
recognized: Lev–Matolcsi, 'The Fuglede conjecture for convex domains is true in all dimensions' (Acta Math. 2022)
